newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED DOWN BUT NOT OUT AFTER JUVENTUS WIN THRILLER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED DOWN BUT NOT OUT AFTER JUVENTUS WIN THRILLER.

text.p: Champions Juventus secured a place in the last eight of the European Cup after beating Manchester United 1-0 in a titanic Champions' League group C match at Old Trafford on Wednesday.
Although the teams produced only one goal between them -- a 35th minute penalty cracked home by Alessandro del Piero -- they created enough chances to have finished the match level at 6-6.

In the end the decisive moment came when Nicky Butt tripped del Piero in the box and although del Piero tumbled theatrically the Spanish referee had no hesitation in awarding a penalty. Del Piero gave United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel no chance with a shot he rifled into the roof of the net.

Juventus, who will now face either arch-rivals AC Milan or Norway's Rosenborg in the quarter-finals next March, were outstanding, with French midfielder Zinedine Zidane running the game for the opening hour.

They gave an almost faultless first-half display that brought lavish praise from United manager Alex Ferguson, whose side can still reach the last eight if they avoid defeat in their last match at Rapid Vienna and Juventus beat Fenerbahce.

Juventus were helped by an early injury that forced United's left-back Philip Neville to limp off with a pulled hamstring after only 12 minutes. Ferguson was forced to re-shuffle his side with Ronny Johnsen going to left back, midfielder Roy Keane dropping into the centre of defence and substitute Brian McClair going into midfield.
Even so, there was little that a full-strength United could have done to contain Juventus at that stage as they gave United a lesson in passing, movement and athleticism.

Ferguson said afterwards: "Juventus were fantastic and they proved tonight, especially in the first half, why they are European champions. Their work ethic was superb, every player earns his money, they have experience and threats in all the right places. I am unhappy with the score, of course, but not unhappy to have taken part in a memorable game of football."

United battled back into the game after halftime and although never quite dominating in the way Juventus had in the early stages, they were unlucky not to gain something from one of a dozen chances they created

Their French skipper Eric Cantona had a golden opportunity to equalise a minute after the break, but saw goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi smother his shot, and late in the game he went close again with a 20-metre drive that bounced off the top of the bar.

In between, David Beckham, Keane, Ole Solskjaer and Ryan Giggs all went close, and Alen Boksic was near for Juventus in the closing minutes, firing wide after breaking free with only Schmeichel to beat.

It was end-to-end football with del Piero, Zidane, Vladimir Jugovic and Moreno Torricelli outstanding for the visitors, who helped conjure memories of some of the great nights of football at Old Trafford.

Unfortunately for the United fans they saw their team lose at home for the second successive European tie in three weeks -- following 40 years in which Old Trafford proved to be an impregnable fortress on European nights.

Juventus coach Marcello Lippi said afterwards he was proud Juventus had become the first Italian side ever to win a competitive match at Old Trafford -- especially after their team coach was caught in a traffic jam and did not arrive at the ground until 30 minutes before kickoff.

"This was a very, very important game for Juventus to win, and I am very proud of my team. There is no question that now we have qualified we will ease up against Fenerbahce in the final game. We do not play like that we play to win."
Those were comforting words to Ferguson, who said: "Juventus play to win every match out of habit. I know they will not ease up against the Turks. Now it is up to us to get a result in Vienna."
Teams:

Manchester United: 1-Peter Schmeichel; 2-Gary Neville, 4-David May, 5-Ronny Johnsen, 28-Philip Neville (13-Brian McClair 13th), 8-Nicky Butt, 10-David Beckham, 7-Eric Cantona, 11-Ryan Giggs, 16-Roy Keane, 20-Ole Solskjaer (14-Jordi Cruyff 81st).

Juventus: 1-Angelo Peruzzi; 5-Sergio Porrini, 2-Ciro Ferrara, 4-Paolo Montero, 3-Moreno Torricelli (13-Mark Juliano 82nd), 21-Zinedine Zidane, 7-Angelo Di Livio (20-Alessio Tacchinardi 79th), 14-Didier Deschamps, 9-Alen Boksic, 18-Vladimir Jugovic, 10-Alessandro del Piero.
Referee: Jose-Maria Garcia-Aranda.
